title:
PROPORTION,
(PROPORTION GRAPHS)
objective: LO: I can identify and interpret graphs showing direct and inverse proportion.

content.text: A direct proportion graph is a straight line through the origin. The gradient equals the constant k.
An inverse proportion graph is a curve (hyperbola) that gets closer to the axes but never touches them.

examples.expr: Inverse proportion is a straight line

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Direct: straight line through origin (y = kx). Inverse: hyperbola (y = k/x). Read k from the graph.
key_idea.equation: Direct: gradient = k | Inverse: xy = k
key_idea.caption: Both can be identified from their graph shape

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – identifying direct proportion
modelled_examples.question: A graph passes through (0,0) and (4, 20). Is it direct proportion? Find k.
steps: Passes through origin: yes, could be direct proportion
modelled_examples.explanation: A straight line through the origin confirms direct proportion.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – reading an inverse graph
modelled_examples.question: A curve passes through (2, 12) and (4, 6). Show this is inverse proportion.
modelled_examples.explanation: If xy is constant for all points, it is inverse proportion.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – from table to graph type
modelled_examples.question: x: 1, 2, 3, 4. y: 5, 10, 15, 20. What type of proportion?
steps: Direct proportion (line through origin with gradient 5)
modelled_examples.explanation: Constant ratio y/x confirms direct proportion.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – from table - inverse
modelled_examples.question: x: 1, 2, 4, 8. y: 40, 20, 10, 5. What type?
modelled_examples.explanation: Constant product xy confirms inverse proportion.

problems.text: A graph passes through the points (2, 8), (4, 4) and (8, 2). (i) Show this is inverse proportion. (ii) Find k. (iii) Predict y when x = 16.
Two variables are tested. x: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y: 3, 12, 27, 48, 75. Is this direct proportion? If not, investigate whether y ∝ x² or another relationship.
